name: Vela
introduction: is the Sails of the ancient ship Argo Navis. It lies in the southern Milky Way and contains many bright stars and remnants of exploded stars.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: About 11,000 years ago, a supernova exploded here, leaving the Vela Supernova Remnant and the [Vela Pulsar](id:psr-j0835m4510), a neutron star spinning 11 times a second. It is one of the brightest gamma-ray sources in the sky and occasionally speeds up suddenly in “glitches”.
Nearby lies [Luhman 16](id:luhman-16-a), a pair of brown dwarfs only 6.5 light-years away, discovered in 2013, the third-nearest system to the Sun.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Regor](hip:39953) is a binary that contains the brightest Wolf–Rayet star, a massive star stripped of its outer layers. [Alsephina](hip:42913) is an eclipsing binary discovered in 2000 by the Galileo spacecraft’s star tracker.
[Suhail](hip:44816) is an orange supergiant, and [Markeb](hip:45941) and Alsephina, with two stars of Carina, form the False Cross. [Mu Velorum](hip:52727) is a yellow giant.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Vela contains the open cluster IC 2391, the Gum Nebula, a huge shell of glowing gas, and the Eight-Burst Nebula, a planetary nebula imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope.
